chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Umar ibn Yazid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

"When the servant performs i'tikaf, he should fast." And he said, "I'tikaf is not valid for less than three days. Make a condition upon your Lord in your i'tikaf as you make a condition in your ihram. Indeed, that is in your i'tikaf in case of an incident, if a cause befalls you from the affair of Allah."

key_terms.إِحْرَام: Ihram (state of consecration, often used by analogy for i'tikaf conditions)

ai.seo_question: What are the minimum duration and fasting requirements for i'tikaf according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the foundational jurisprudence of i'tikaf, linking the spiritual retreat directly to the obligation of fasting, a view emphasized in Shia fiqh. It introduces the concept of 'shart al-gharar' (conditioning against uncertainty), allowing the worshipper to stipulate that their i'tikaf remains valid if interrupted by illness or other divine decrees, thereby ensuring the continuity of their worship despite unforeseen events.
